steps.title: Import Vue and required APIs (ref, computed, defineComponent)
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref, computed, and defineComponent from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue APIs. The syntax is: import { ... } from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple functions from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue, ref, computed, and defineComponent from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and required APIs are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue, ref, computed, and defineComponent are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and the required APIs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but check that you've imported all required APIs: Vue, ref, computed, and defineComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Ensure you import Vue, ref, computed, and defineComponent from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component using defineComponent with an empty setup function. Name the component 'DeferredValueDemo'.
steps.hint: Use defineComponent to define a component object with a setup function that returns an empty object for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component 'DeferredValueDemo' is defined with defineComponent and an empty setup function.
successCriteria: A component named 'DeferredValueDemo' is exported using defineComponent with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using defineComponent with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using defineComponent with a setup function.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for input value
steps.instruction: In the setup function, create a ref called 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create reactive state. Import ref if you haven't already, then declare const inputValue = ref('') inside setup.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state with ref
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have reactive state to track user input.
successCriteria: A ref named inputValue is declared inside setup and initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created reactive state to track the input value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref and initializing it with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the setup function. You need to declare a ref called inputValue with an initial value of ''.

steps.title: Create computed property for deferred value
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a computed property called 'deferredValue' that returns the inputValue with a simulated delay using setTimeout.
steps.hint: Use the computed function from Vue to create a reactive computed property. Inside the computed getter, you can use setTimeout to delay returning the value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a computed property 'deferredValue' that will reactively update with a delay when inputValue changes.
successCriteria: A computed property named 'deferredValue' is created inside the setup function and uses setTimeout to delay returning inputValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the deferredValue computed property with simulated delay.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a computed property, but make sure it's named 'deferredValue' and includes a setTimeout to delay returning the inputValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property 'deferredValue' with simulated delay wasn't created correctly. Check the syntax for computed properties and setTimeout.

steps.title: Add input handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named 'handleInput' that takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue ref with the event target's value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives an event object and sets inputValue.value to event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleInput function that updates the reactive inputValue when called with an input event.
successCriteria: A function named handleInput is defined inside setup, takes an event parameter, and sets inputValue.value to event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleInput function that will update the input value when the user types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named handleInput, takes an event parameter, and updates inputValue.value with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInput function is missing or incorrect. It should update inputValue.value with the event's target value.

steps.title: Return reactive values and handlers from setup
steps.instruction: Return the inputValue, deferredValue, and handleInput from the setup function so they can be used in the template.
steps.hint: In Vue's setup function, you return an object containing all the reactive values and methods you want to expose to the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object containing inputValue, deferredValue, and handleInput, making them available to the component's template.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with inputValue, deferredValue, and handleInput properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned all the reactive values and handlers from the setup function. Now they can be accessed in the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with all three properties: inputValue, deferredValue, and handleInput.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function needs to return an object containing inputValue, deferredValue, and handleInput so they can be used in the template.

steps.title: Add template structure with input field
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your component with an input element bound to inputValue using v-model.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can add a template section with the <template> tag. Use v-model to bind the input element to your inputValue ref.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: template with input binding
<template>
  <input v-model="inputValue" />
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template section containing an input field that updates the inputValue state when typed into.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the template structure with an input field bound to your reactive state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the template section and the input element with v-model binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't complete. Remember to add a template section with an input element using v-model.

steps.title: Display current input value
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph element that displays the current input value. Use double curly braces to show inputValue.
steps.hint:
Add a

tag with {{ inputValue }} inside the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a reactive value in a paragraph

{{ message }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a paragraph element that will display the current value of inputValue in the UI.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with {{ inputValue }} is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a paragraph that will display the current input value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it uses {{ inputValue }} to display the reactive value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or does not display inputValue correctly.

steps.title: Display deferred value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element in your template to display the deferredValue computed property.
steps.hint: Use the same syntax as the previous paragraph but reference deferredValue instead of inputValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a second paragraph showing the deferred value, which currently matches the input value.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays the deferredValue computed property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the paragraph to display the deferred value. This will help visualize the difference once we add the deferral logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the deferredValue computed property in a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph for deferredValue isn't present yet. Add a

element that shows the deferredValue.

steps.title: Add explanatory text and styling
steps.instruction: Add labels and basic inline styling to distinguish between the immediate and deferred values in your template.
steps.hint: Add descriptive text before each value and use the style attribute to give them different colors.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding labels and styling

Label: {{ value }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show clear labels and visual differentiation between the immediate input value and the deferred value.
successCriteria: The template includes labels for both values and uses inline styling to give them different colors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added explanatory text and styling to help distinguish between the immediate and deferred values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added labels for both values and applied different colors using the style attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add descriptive text before each value and use inline styling to give them different visual appearances.
